subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should ACP `sessions_spawn` be allowed to copy OpenClaw skill context into external ACP harness prompts, and if so which selection modes, redaction/audit fields, and parity constraints are supported?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but implementation decides whether trusted local skill content may cross into external harness prompts and how that interacts with existing native/Codex skill contracts.

options.title: Start Explicit-Only With Audit
options.body: Add only an explicit skill-id selector first, with redaction, prompt-size limits, source hashes, and observable child load/invocation metadata before considering auto/default modes.

options.title: Defer To Skill-Contract Parity
options.body: Keep ACP skill injection blocked until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95058 settles the owning prompt layer and lifetime semantics.

options.title: Keep ACP Isolated
options.body: Reject core skill injection and require users to use native harness skills, MCP bridges, or plugin-specific mechanisms instead.

recommendation.title: Start Explicit-Only With Audit
recommendation.body: Add only an explicit skill-id selector first, with redaction, prompt-size limits, source hashes, and observable child load/invocation metadata before considering auto/default modes.

likelyOwner.reason: The ACP thread-bound agent feature history originates in osolmaz's central ACP commit, making them the best available owner signal for the initial contract decision.
